contradictions.severity: resolved in favour of live caller evidence
contradictions.source: derived ABI record (categories.abi_derived.value.return.register_class, and abi.return_semantics): the last value written to EAX classifies as `pointer_like`
contradictions.conflicting_evidence: live decompilation of seven sampled callers: 0x00bd0000, 0x00bf0f40, 0x00bd7160, 0x00cf78d0, 0x00bf1fd0, 0x00bf9820, 0x00d07e40. Every one treats the result as an enum-like small integer; NONE dereferences it.
evidence_quotes: 0x00bf0f40: iVar1 = FUN_00bd81d0(); if (iVar1 != 0) { if (iVar1 == 1) return 2; if (iVar1 != 2) return -1; return 1; } return 0;
0x00bd0000: iVar3 = FUN_00bd81d0(); if (iVar3 == 1) {...} else if (iVar3 == 2) {...} else {...}
0x00bf1fd0: iVar1 = FUN_00bd81d0(); if (iVar1 == param_2) { ... arithmetic on iVar1 ... }
contradictions.resolution: The record's label is a register-shape heuristic on a 32-bit EAX value, not a use observation. A 32-bit word is shape-compatible with a pointer, which is presumably what the heuristic fires on. This package models the return as a 32-bit integer and records the disagreement rather than adopting or dropping the label silently. Model test group 2 is the check that holds the line: the four observed comparands and the 32-bit extremes must all come back bit-identical.
contradictions.residual_risk: If some UNSAMPLED caller does dereference the returned word, a pointer reading would also fit. The sample is 7 of 31 distinct callers. This is stated rather than ruled out.

semantic_findings: The entry is a receiver-relative integer field accessor: one 32-bit load, one return, no validation, no default, no write.
The field it reads is at +0x540 on its receiver and is UNNAMED; the class that owns the receiver is UNKNOWN.

The returned value behaves as an enum-like small integer across every sampled caller: the literal comparands 0, 1, 2 and -1 all appear, and 0x00bf0f40 performs an explicit remap 0->0, 1->2, 2->1, other->-1.

0x00bd7160's comparison against -1 is the one observation that would also be consistent with a signed enum domain; the body performs no sign extension, so the value is carried as a raw 32-bit bit pattern and the return type is modelled as unsigned. No enum type and no enumerator name is claimed.

The enclosing accessor block (0x00bd8190..0x00bd81f0) is a run of tiny ECX-relative members mixing readers and writers, so the receiver is a real multi-field object and the accessor family is a shared one.
0x00bd81a0 is `LEA EAX,[ECX + 0x548]` - the load-versus-LEA contrast is present in this very block, so a LEA-form reading of this target is a live failure mode rather than a hypothetical one.
72 xrefs from 31 distinct caller functions, 0 callees: a shared accessor. Fan-in is used here only to justify that description and is not evidence for any identity.
not_claimed: The class of the receiver at +0x540. UNKNOWN; the type is opaque and asserts no Simulator class.
The name, domain, enumerator names or meaning of the field at +0x540. UNNAMED.
Any SDK symbol for this entry. Ghidra's SDK import left it FUN_00bd81d0.
That the field is never written anywhere in the image. This body does not write it; no writer for +0x540 was located and absence was not established.
Any writer, publication order, nullability, thread-safety or ownership for the receiver or the field.
Any calling convention observable from this function alone; __thiscall is the record's resolution of an ambiguity this body cannot settle.
The size or full layout of the receiver beyond the one offset the body reaches and the sibling offsets the block scan observed.
Any virtual dispatch, tail call, variadic behaviour or struct return. Each is measured at zero/absent and the two-instruction listing agrees.
Any runtime, Wine, trace, differential or OBSERVED-behaviour claim. No runtime evidence exists for this VA.

unresolved_questions: What class owns offset 0x540, and what is the field called? No SDK import, namespace or committed research note names either. Ghidra left the entry FUN_00bd81d0.

Who writes +0x540, and when relative to the 31 distinct caller functions that read it? No writer was located for this offset; the sibling writers found in the block cover +0x33c and +0x2f0 only. This is an unlocated writer, NOT an established absence.
What are the enumerators? The 0/1/2/-1 comparands establish an enum-like domain and nothing more. The -1 at 0x00bd7160 suggests a signed domain, but no name, count or ordering is evidenced.
Do the remaining 24 unsampled caller functions ever dereference the returned word? If one does, a pointer reading also fits and the contradiction above would reopen.

Is the receiver the same object the sibling block members at +0x2f8, +0x548, +0x21c, +0x33c and +0x2f0 belong to? The shared ECX and the 0x10 spacing make it likely but nothing names the class, so the block's members are NOT claimed as this receiver's siblings.
Is there a setter counterpart to this getter elsewhere in the image (as 0x00bd81e0 pairs with 0x00bd81f0 for +0x2f0)? Not searched; this package is bounded to the target and its immediate block.

focused_test.assertion_style: abort on the first failure; each group names the hypothesis it refutes
coverage: the return is the word stored at +0x540, not the member's address, not the offset, not a constant, not zero

the return is a verbatim scalar: the four observed comparands 0/1/2/-1 and the 32-bit extremes 0xffffffff, 0x7fffffff, 0x80000000, 0xffff, 0x10000, 0xabcdef01 all come back bit-identical, which is the check that holds the line against the ABI record's pointer_like label
the offset is exactly 0x540: guard words planted one word below and one word above are neither returned nor disturbed, and each is planted with a distinct value in turn
the body reads: the whole 0x548-byte receiver is byte-identical before and after the call
a pure function of the field: repeats, tracks every change, returns a stored zero unchanged, returns each observed comparand unchanged
the receiver IS ECX, read off the encoding: opcode 0x8b, ModRM 0x81 decoded as mod=10 / reg=000 (EAX) / r/m=001 (ECX), with the SIB escapes r/m=100 and r/m=101 named so a substituted ModRM is caught
the callee pops nothing: the trailing byte is 0xc3 (RET, no imm16) and not 0xc2/0xca/0xcb, named against the RET 4 form the sibling writers in the same block use
the encoding is the observed seven bytes and its disp32 reassembles to the header's kSlotOffset
the modelled entry is a zero-argument member returning one 32-bit word, so a reconstruction that grew a stack argument could not be declared against it
focused_test.abi_claim_basis: encoding, not run-time sampling. A sibling package in this repository sampled ESP around the call and re-called from a deeper frame via constrained inline asm; every version of that measurement was silently unreliable across -O levels and compilers (a callee-saved register allocated to an output and then overwritten by the harness's own `pop`, a variable alloca folded into one fixed frame so both depths were the same point, and a `call *%reg` whose target register the compiler allocated to the register being poisoned). For a body of `8b 81 <disp32>; c3` the ModRM byte states the base register outright and the encoding argument holds identically at every optimisation level, so the measurement was not used. This is recorded in the test file's header comment.
focused_test.build_matrix: g++ and clang++, -m32, -Wall -Wextra -Werror, -std=c++17, at -O0/-O1/-O2/-O3: all 8 configurations pass
focused_test.mutation_harness: /tmp/opencode/mut00bd81d0/run_mutations.sh - each mutation is applied to a fresh COPY of the package in its own directory and the harness compiles from INSIDE that directory, so #include resolves the MUTATED header. The archive is deleted and rebuilt with `ar rc` before every link; `ar qc` is never used, because it APPENDS and a stale object from a previous mutant would silently win the link and make a mutation appear undetected.
